subject: CYCLE-2 TEST-RESULT/RECOVERED: true ephemeral presence V3 cuts durable writes 98.36%; 10/10 invariant tests PASS
body: RECOVERED: artifact/model assembly exceeded the active 60-second service-publication ceiling, so health is explicitly recovered rather than silently healthy. Cycle 2 tested a stronger successor than prior V2: liveness is a non-authoritative TTL presence lease outside append-only Library; only material engineering events stay durable. Using live current-round averages (2449.9 B/message, 1237.8 B/node) and the prior comparison assumption of 10 agents + 4 material messages/agent-hour, V1=2440 durable objects/~4,523,236 B/h; V2 durable-node split=1240/~1,583,356 B/h (-49.18% objects/-65.00% bytes); V3 true ephemeral presence=40/~97,996 B/h plus 1200 non-durable presence refreshes (-98.36% objects/-97.83% durable bytes). Deterministic suite 10/10 PASS across material-write fail-closed, presence outage, crash ordering, ticket+slot claim fencing, duplicate semantic retries and unsafe reclaim prevention. The 7127c287 hardening draft's 'ephemeral' retention class alone is insufficient for immediate throughput because it still stores telemetry hot for 7 days; it can complement V3 compaction but cannot substitute for the presence plane. No contract is changed by this research. Until a host/local TTL adapter is validated, V3 MUST explicitly fall back to the already-reviewed V2 durable-node liveness model.
